--- Begin excerpt ---
Redwood Inference — Switchover Ownership & RTO/RPO (Warm-standby profile)

Ownership model: Redwood provides operational tooling and automated routing controls to perform a cross-region switchover. The customer retains final authorization to execute a region-wide activation unless an agreed automated failover policy is enabled (customer can opt-in to automated failover for predefined catastrophic conditions). All switchover decisions are recorded in the Redwood Control Plane audit log with timestamp, initiating principal, and policy version.

RTO / RPO commitments:
- Warm-standby (recommended): Typical observed RTO 5-15 minutes for API-level traffic re-routing when KV caches are warm; nominal RPO < 30s for non-batched persistent stores (dependent on customer replication window).
- Cold failover / full rebuild: RTO varies; can exceed hours depending on snapshot restoration and model weight transfer — not recommended for latency-sensitive workloads.

Notes / caveats:
- RTO is a function of: regional network ramp-up, active connections teardown, KV cache warmup (we provide cache pre-warm tooling), and size of model checkpoints to rehydrate (quantized weights reduce transfer time).
- Where customers require stricter RTO/RPO, Redwood recommends dedicated capacity and synchronous replication across regions; we can propose the quantization/profile that minimizes transfer size.

--- End excerpt ---

Attachments: runbook-excerpt.md (short activation checklist)

Ben

Adding a runbook excerpt you can paste under "Activation Procedures":

--- Runbook excerpt ---
Activation checklist (warm-standby -> active)
1) Confirm incident classification and trigger authorization (owner: customer ops or delegated admin).
2) Initiate control-plane activation: set region routing policy to "activate" and note policy id.
3) Verify model artifact integrity on target region (checksum).
4) Warm KV cache using pre-warm API for top-k prefixes (parallel pre-warm to reduce cold-cache penalty).
5) Start traffic ramp: 10% / 30 min -> 50% / 1 hr -> full, monitor latency and error-rate.
6) Post-activation validation: token-level tracing for 15 minutes, confirm no data drift and consistent embeddings.

Steps that extend RTO: full checkpoint transfer, manual approval gating, and any required customer-side routing DNS TTLs >60s.

Marissa

Sofia,

Compliance text for data guardrails (short form):

Data residency & replication controls: Redwood allows customers to scope model artifacts and user data to specific cloud regions and to exclude target jurisdictions via replication policies. Cross-region replication is configurable (asynchronous by default) and may be restricted to a set of approved regions to meet data residency requirements.

Encryption & transport: All inter-region replication and control-plane traffic is encrypted with TLS 1.3. Model artifacts at rest are encrypted using customer-managed keys (KMS) where requested. Audit logs and control-plane events are retained per the customer’s contract and support retention add-ons.

Evidence: SOC2 Type II report and control mapping available (see linked Drive folder). For customers requiring contract language, we can provide specific clauses that map to AegisBank policy upon request.
